subject: Ephemeral streaming slowdown — status, temporary mitigations, and next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Desai <samir@finpay.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Ephemeral streaming slowdown — status, temporary mitigations, and next steps

Hi Samir,

Thanks for flagging the degraded response cadence this morning — I wanted to share what we've confirmed so far and the immediate steps our ops team has taken. Short summary up front: between ~07:40 and 08:30 PT we observed elevated tail latency on the streaming/chat endpoint for a subset of requests in the us-west region. Impact: visible pauses (~1–5s extra per chunk) when sending streaming tokens to clients behind socket connections.

What we've done already (short-term fixes applied):
- Rolled a temporary token-emission smoothing config to affected hosts to reduce microburst pressure.
- Reduced batch window from 25ms -> 15ms on the shard serving your traffic to prioritize latency vs throughput.
- Prioritized prefix cache warming for hot customer keys (FinPay used this morning) to avoid cold KV lookups.

We expect these mitigations to reduce the pause frequency immediately. We're also collecting per-connection traces and token timing windows to validate. Can you confirm if you saw a clear user-visible regression during the 07:40—08:30 window and whether the timestamps below match any FinPay session IDs? If you can forward any sample session IDs or logs, that will speed the triage.

Sample timestamps we saw in our traces: 2026-11-27T07:41:12Z, 2026-11-27T07:53:04Z, 2026-11-27T08:07:38Z.

Attached are a snapshot of the latency traces and a CSV of token-level emission metrics we captured.

Next steps from Redwood:
- Ben is owning immediate telemetry correlation and will provide a short postmortem by EOD.
- Karthik is evaluating whether a kernel-level backpressure regression on the new batching path contributed.
- We'll schedule a 30-minute bridge for tomorrow morning to go over logs and a remediation plan if you'd like.

We're treating this as a high priority; apologies for the disruption. I will update you as we confirm root cause.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Ephemeral streaming slowdown — status, temporary mitigations, and next steps

Quick tech update and proposed customer-facing actions:

What we found (early):
- Telemetry shows short-lived token-emission queue growth on a subset of hosts running the new batching kernel. The growth correlates with a recent autoscaler smoothing change deployed 2026-11-25 that delayed eviction of warm worker slots by ~3s under microbursts. That smoothing decreased churn but increased tail queueing under bursty interactive loads.
- Only a narrow slice of traffic (clients pinned to shard-17 in us-west) hit the worst tail effects — FinPay traffic overlapped with the hot prefix set.

Immediate plan (24h):
1) Keep reduced batch-window (15ms) on shard-17 and revert the autoscaler smoothing change for the affected host pool to remove the ~3s retention. Expected effect: remove most queue accumulation and restore per-chunk parity within 1–2 hours after revert.
2) Run a targeted canary for the reverted autoscaler change on one host group with stress testing to ensure no regression to churn.
3) Provide FinPay a 1-week credit for any sustained 99th percentile latency above baseline while we complete the root cause analysis — I will coordinate with LAURA on wording.

Customer comms guidance (Laura):
- Publish an incident note that: (a) describes observed impact, (b) lists mitigations we applied, (c) commits to a follow-up with root cause analysis in 72 hours and (d) invites them to the bridge tomorrow at 09:00 PT. Avoid deep technical conjecture; stick to facts and timelines.

Longer-term (1–3 weeks):
- Karthik, estimate effort to make the autoscaler smoothing parameter adaptive (hot-prefix-aware) to avoid this tradeoff.
- Engineering will add an alert that detects rapid queue growth on batching kernels with a per-shard scope.

I'll send a short external summary now and the invite once we lock triage owners.

Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
